_about: The Five Trials of the prologue, and the other work tasks of the story (kind: task, with no calling): work in the village, one task for each calling (src/core/world/trials.js and src/core/world/systems/work.js). The talk of the person starts the task in the world ({ open: 'trial', id }); the task is done when the world says so, and then the flag is set, the reward flies to the counters, and the person says the done line (dialogue <npc>.trial.done, or doneTalk). grades: the level of the task (1, 2, or 3) for the grade that the player gave (the nearest grade for others). levels: the numbers of the task at each level, and the skill that the task measures at that level (one skill event at each commit). The stakes of the fisher and the marks of the woodcutter are lengths on a line, as the planks of the bridge: they share the number-line skill of the bridge (math.add.20, the sum skill in data/world/zones.json). places: the named places of the map (layers.places) where the things of the task lie. Units: half blocks (one map cell is 2) and seconds. No numeral is shown in the world; a person says a number in words (the key num.<n>).

trials._task: Sort the counting rods into bundles of ten for the teacher. A tap on a rod of the heap puts it on the mat (from near the mat). A tap on the straw rope by the mat ties the rods on the mat: ten rods tie into a bundle; more or fewer, and the band snaps and the rods fall back on the heap (the commit). The task is done when fewer than ten rods are left on the heap.

The fire burns when the child comes: the ore is in the forge (this many lumps) and the water is in the trough. The smith quenches one piece himself first. Then the iron on the anvil glows (rise), stays hot (hold), and dims (dim), again and again. The action button at the anvil drops the iron into the water (the commit): while it is hot (glow at or over hot), it hisses and becomes hard; too early or too late, it bends and goes back into the fire. From grade 3 (#102) the iron goes through its colors in the fire (colors: the seconds of dark red, cherry red, orange, yellow, and the cool time out of the fire), and no pulse says when: a quench at cherry red is right, and the smith says the color of a piece that bends. The task has pieces of a number (pieces), one at a time. water (grade 4): the steam over the trough grows with each piece, and after warmAfter pieces the warm water leaves a piece soft, until the child pours a pail from the jar into the trough. fair (grade 5): two pieces from the same fire, one into the water and one onto the rack; the smith bends both, and the record keeps whether only one thing changed (fair); then the rest of the pieces.

A fish trap: stakes in a row in the river, from the first stake to the end mark, before the tide comes in. The fisher puts the first two stakes, so the space between them shows the space of the row. The child carries stakes from the bank and puts each one on the line (it snaps to the half-block grid), and can take one back. When the tide comes in (tide: seconds after the start, and again after each tide), the row is the commit: no space between two stakes wider than the space of the row, and the last stake at the end mark. Then the tide goes out: the fish stay in the trap, or they swim out through the widest space. The fewest stakes is efficient. From grade 3 (#102) the stakes go into a boat at the pile (each press puts one stake into it), and a tap on the boat sends it: it brings the stakes in one trip and sets them at the gap of the row from the last stake. The load is the commit. measure (grade 3): the gap is one pole (pole: half blocks), and the row is k poles from the stake of the fisher (k stakes); trees (grade 4): k poles from the bank, with a stake at each end (k + 1 stakes); half (grade 5): a gap of one pole and a half, and a row of x poles from the bank (halves: the length in half poles; x ÷ 1,5 + 1 stakes). A press at the row lays the pole one length further. Each level can have its own lines of the talk (talk: a key, or { key, names }).

Three kinds of herbs grow in three beds. The healer needs each (this many) of each kind. The child carries herbs to the basket (each kind goes to its part of the basket) and can take one back. A tap on the healer gives the basket (the commit): every part has each, or the healer gives the basket back and the herbs over the number fly back to their beds.

A fallen bamboo stem lies on the ground (length). The woodcutter needs it in this many equal sticks (parts). A tap on the stem puts a chalk mark there (it snaps to the half-block grid), and a tap on a mark takes it away. A tap on the woodcutter cuts at the marks (the commit): equal sticks are tied into a bundle, and the child carries it to the wood pile by the bridge; sticks that are not equal break, and a new stem comes. From grade 3 (#102) the stem has parts: unit (grade 3): one part of the stem for the bridge (one half, one third, one fourth, or one sixth of a stem of stems rings, as the rings allow), and the rest stays; equiv (grade 4): a/b of the stem for the bridge (fracs), and the rest for stakes; unlike (grade 5): one third for the bridge, one fourth for the fence, and the rest for the kitchen (12 or 24 rings). Each piece is compared with the length that the task asks for. The check of the woodcutter lays a piece along another, one time after another, and says the part.

The iron horse for Gióng. The iron that the child found lies in a heap by the forge, with some old iron of the smith. The child carries lumps into the hearth and takes lumps out again, then taps the bellows (the commit of the count): with the lumps that the smith needs, the fire burns high and the iron goes on the anvil; with too few, the fire puffs and dies; with too many, the fire chokes and the extra rolls back to the heap. Then the iron glows and dims as in the trial of the smith, and a tap drops it into the water: at the right moment it becomes the iron horse.
trials._goals: The goal bar at each part of the forge (#140): the lumps go into the hearth, the fire, the quench.

trials._task: Bamboo staffs for the men of the village before the general comes. A clump of standing bamboo grows by the big road in front of the đình: parts culms in a row, each of height (half blocks), with a ring at each half block. The child walks to a culm and slashes it at the height of the hand (a ring from 1 up to reach), one culm at a time, at once: no chalk, and no taking back. A sample staff of length (rings) stands at the head of the row: each staff must be as long as it, so that the lowest cut is too short and the child must look at the rings (#54). The top falls away, and the piece from the ground to the cut (a staff, as long as the height of the cut) stands where the culm stood, next to the others. When each culm is cut, the pieces are the commit: pieces as long as the sample tie into a bundle of staffs; if not, the pieces of another length break, and their culms grow again. The woodcutter's own trial (a stem on the ground, with chalk) stays as it is.

The loot after a won raid (loot in data/raids.json): a pile of small sacks of rice behind the wall (Era 1 has no coins, #26), and three mats: the basket of the hero, Nghé, and Gióng. The child carries sacks from the pile to the mats, and from a mat back. When the hands are empty and the pile has fewer sacks than friends, and the pile cannot even out the mats, the share is the commit: equal mats make all happy, and the sacks of the hero go to the basket as measures of rice; if not, Nghé turns away and sulks until the share is fair. The rest in the pile (fewer sacks than friends) becomes a small red cloth with the sacks in the hands of the hero: the child carries it to the village, to one of the people of rest (the elder at the đình, the smith, or the mother of Gióng), and the person says one line of thanks. The cloth goes with the hero to other maps; nothing is scored.

Rice for Gióng (not a trial of a calling: a task of the story). Trays of 3 and of 5 bowls of rice lie on the path of the paddies (trays: the sizes; each size has this many trays, and a tray that goes to the pot comes back full to the path). The child carries one tray at a time to the pot in front of the house of Gióng. Each ten bowls: Gióng eats and grows one head taller; the bowls over the ten stay in the pot (the ones), and his height shows the tens. The commit is each ten: solved when the pot comes to exactly ten, efficient with the fewest trays for it. The task is done when Gióng has grown this many heads. pace: the speed factor of the walk with a tray of that size: a tray of five is heavy, so the fewest trays is not always the fastest. Each tray at the pot goes into the learning log (the kind carry: the size and the seconds of the walk).
